HOLDING, and stacked on 2.9.0's unreleased hold -- but for its own reason, not 2.9.0's: unconditional x-schema-version holding is scoped to nested-field-additive/enum-value-additive/major, NOT to top-level-array-additive, which is non-holding only where a declared-tolerant consumer set exists. No structural or version-envelope tolerance is declared for claude-klabauter's vendored copy, so this reverts to bilateral sequencing and holds anyway (docs/wiki/schema-version-gate.md) -- merge-to-main and production emit are held until claude-klabauter re-vendors or confirms plan.schema.json is not in their mirrored set. 2.9.0's notification (cross-repo/inbox/2026-08-27-doe-claude-em-plan-schema-2-9-0-nested-field-additive) is unanswered; 2.10.0 owes its own. The falsifier object is `additionalProperties: false`, so a plan recording either shape failed validation against 2.8.0. The two branches are mutually exclusive and `promotion_reason` is dependent-required on `promotion`; promotability stays a record, never a gate on the stamp. HOLDING: nested-field-additive is unconditionally holding on the x-schema-version axis (docs/wiki/schema-version-gate.md) -- merge-to-main and production emit are held until claude-klabauter re-vendors or confirms plan.schema.json is not in their mirrored set. description: Plan frontmatter schema. The active-execution value is 'executing', NOT the intuitive 'execution'. 'implemented' means work is done on the working branch — whether it merged to main is tracked in completion log + handoff deployment_state, NOT here.

author.description: Agent or person who authored this plan.

status.description: Lifecycle state. Common slip: active-execution value is 'executing', NOT 'execution'. 'landed' sits between 'executing' and 'implemented': every chunk's code is on the branch, but not every spine row has reached a disposition yet. It is NOT terminal — a plan in 'landed' still has outstanding row-level work to close out before it can move to 'implemented'.

branch.description: Working branch this plan is being executed on.

source.description: Origin reference (e.g. a handoff slug, memo path, or external prompt).

superseded_by.description: Path or slug of the plan that supersedes this one.

scope_mode.description: Planning posture (e.g. 'architecture', 'implementation', 'spike', 'spec-dispatch' — the S-lane posture routed from coordinator:sizing: a light plan artifact scaffolded then dispatched, skipping the Opus plan review).

problem_set.description: Ratified problem-set slug or inline statement (from /shape).

predecessor_handoff.description: The handoff that spawned this plan (distinct from parent_plan). Nullable, for the same reason sizing_object is: an explicit null is the sanctioned 'this plan has no resolvable predecessor handoff' answer — a forced declaration rather than an omission, which is what makes the absence checkable. Written with an inline reason naming why (target never authored, or archived-then-pruned). 42 rows were set this way on 2026-08-14; the disposition ledger is state/audits/2026-08-13-predecessor-handoff-fk-disposition.md. A non-null value is expected to resolve on disk, literally or archive-relative — the FK is archive-agnostic by design and readers resolve archive-relative (docs/decisions/DR-159-predecessor-handoff-fk-is-archive-agnostic-by-design.md), so a value resolving only under archive/ is correct, not broken. Referential integrity is enforced by coordinator/tests/test_archive_handoff_referrer_guard.py.

prerequisite_of.description: Downstream plan(s) that depend on this plan completing first.

source_memo.description: Cross-repo memo(s) that initiated this plan. May be a single path or a list.

scope.description: In-scope items for this plan (list-of-string preferred; legacy string values accepted).

agent_sessions.description: Sessions that executed this plan. Runtime-appended by append-plan-session.sh after a successful plan claim (execute-plan Phase 1.5 Step 0); NOT scaffolded onto new plans. Each entry is the encoded string "<session_id>|<status>|<created_at>": session_id is UUID-shaped (contains no '|'); status is an OPEN string ('working' at the Phase-0 fire point, not a closed enum); created_at is ISO-8601 UTC. All three fields are non-empty at write time — consumers must NOT use `IFS='|' read -ra` if a future field could be empty (read -ra silently drops trailing empty fields). Append-only: never rewrite or reorder peer entries.

deliverable_id.description: Durable deliverable join key. Minted once at the earliest artifact and carried verbatim by every downstream artifact. dlv-<stub_id> for roadmap-stub origins; dlv-<slug>-<6hex> for standalone plan origins. Cross-field rule enforces 'dlv-' prefix when non-null. Null for pre-backfill plans. Spec backlink: claude-klabauter:pln-fleet-deliverable-spine-identity-and-facets-2b331c § D1

sizing_object.description: FK to the sizing-object (state/sizings/<id>.yaml) that routed this plan through coordinator:sizing. Optional and nullable in this schema; the requirement is enforced READ-SIDE in claude-klabauter (coordinator_core/ops/assert_plan_sizing_citation.py), never here. A plan created on/after 2026-08-06 must carry EITHER a resolving state/sizings/<id>.yaml path OR an explicit null — explicit null is the sanctioned 'no sizing object' answer, a forced declaration rather than a bypass, which is what makes the absence checkable at all. Plans created before that cutoff are permanently exempt and must NOT be backfilled: the large majority of the on-disk corpus predates the convention, and requiring it of them would invalidate the corpus. When present, the referenced file is expected to resolve on disk. Frontmatter-only: this field is never read from plan BODY prose, and no check compares its value against the plan's problem restatement — a body-scanning or intent-matching variant is out of scope by design (it fires on a plan that legitimately documents an absent or reworded citation). Bilaterally mirrored with claude-klabauter's vendored copy; originating request: state/memo-outbox/sent/plan-sizing-citation-unenforced-at-write-time.md.

plan_id.description: Stable non-path plan identity (pln-<slug>-<6hex>). Minted by coordinator-doc-new at plan creation time. Allows the board to join on a stable key independent of file path/rename. Distinct from deliverable_id (which spans the full deliverable chain). Spec backlink: claude-klabauter:pln-fleet-deliverable-spine-identity-and-facets-2b331c § D3

initiative.description: FK to the initiative entity (state/initiatives/<id>.yaml). Nullable — not all work belongs to a named initiative. Cross-field rule enforces non-empty string when non-null. Spec backlink: claude-klabauter:pln-fleet-deliverable-spine-identity-and-facets-2b331c § D2

caption.description: One-sentence business-legible outcome line. NOT an engineering title or filename — authored for CEO-board legibility. Optional; authored at creation time.

status_reason.description: Free-text one-liner explaining the current plan status (e.g. 'deferred — blocked on cockpit reader-first gate'). Optional authored field; carried into the cockpit emission as a product-legibility facet.

owner.description: Authoring workstream or EM identifier. Nullable; carried forward from the earliest artifact for the deliverable.

suggested_priority.description: Advisory execution-priority signal an EM may attach to this plan at authoring time. Optional (not nullable — absence already covers 'no suggestion'; a redundant null representation was reviewed out, see Finding 4 / review-integrator). Enum is the priority-ledger domain (priority-ledger.schema.json's urgent|high|medium|low|none) MINUS 'none' — an EM has no reason to author an explicit clear; absence of the field already covers that case. Advisory only: the PM-owned priority ledger (state/priority-ledger/) is the authoritative tier and lives on a deliberately separate surface — this field never overrides it, and that separation (not memory) is what keeps 'advisory never overrides authoritative' structural. Do NOT add a pm_priority field to this frontmatter to compensate; the tier split is the point. NEGATIVE-SPEC: no inherited_from / priority_predecessor field is permitted on this frontmatter either — priority does not chain plan-to-plan. No backfill of pre-existing plans, consistent with the handoff schema's origin_* no-backfill policy.

provisional_until.description: Expiry date (YYYY-MM-DD) for a decision this plan stages but does not yet execute — e.g. a ratification, a second stage of a two-stage rollout, or a hold pending a future condition. `revisit_by` is an accepted synonym key (same semantics, same format); a plan carries one or the other, never both. Read by the outstanding-provisional-decisions ceremony check (`coordinator/docs/wiki/provisional-decision-expiry.md`) against every non-terminal-status plan (`status` not in implemented/deferred/abandoned/superseded) — a date on or before today with the plan still non-terminal is surfaced as expired. Motivating case: the 2026-07-13 adopt spec's stage-2 ratification sat unexecuted for 13 days with nothing tracking that it was owed (archive/specs/2026-07/2026-07-13-doe-auto-reconcile-adopt.md). Optional; null/absent for plans that stage no provisional decision. Spec backlink: pln-push-side-write-discipline-for-05c30d § D1b.

revisit_by.description: Synonym key for `provisional_until` — same semantics, same format, same consumer. Use whichever name reads more naturally at the call site (`revisit_by` for a park_note-style hold; `provisional_until` for a staged-decision expiry); a plan sets at most one of the two. See `provisional_until` for the full description.

tasks.description: NOT a frontmatter key — the ## Tasks task-spine lives BODY-RESIDENT in a single fenced ```yaml plan-tasks``` code block directly under the ## Tasks heading (parser-locate rule: exactly one such block; zero or >1 is a defined error). This 'tasks' property exists to WIRE the per-row shape (schemas/plan-tasks.schema.json) into the plan schema family for validators that parse the fenced block's YAML list and want the item schema, per the canonical body-resident-machine-block pattern (docs/wiki/canonical-artifact-shapes.md § Addressable-Section Convention, rule 4 — cf. the ## Session Ledger precedent in handoffs). Full authoring contract: docs/wiki/writing-plans.md § Machine-Parseable Task Spine. Spec backlink: pln-full-coverage-planning-posture-bca96f § C1.

execution_authorized_by.description: The PM/session that authorized execution. OPTIONAL — one of the four-field execution-authorization stamp (by/at/sha/note), mirrored from handoff.schema.json's identically-named field for the plan→execute-plan Stop-hook seam. Spec backlink: pln-first-class-execution-handoff--40a6e5 § C1

execution_authorized_at.description: ISO 8601 date-time of authorization. OPTIONAL — one of the four-field execution-authorization stamp (by/at/sha/note), mirrored from handoff.schema.json's identically-named field for the plan→execute-plan Stop-hook seam. Spec backlink: pln-first-class-execution-handoff--40a6e5 § C1

execution_authorized_sha.description: git-hash-object of the plan body at authorization (the content-binding witness /pickup recomputes; schema shape-only). OPTIONAL — one of the four-field execution-authorization stamp (by/at/sha/note), mirrored from handoff.schema.json's identically-named field for the plan→execute-plan Stop-hook seam. Spec backlink: pln-first-class-execution-handoff--40a6e5 § C1

execution_authorized_note.description: The verbatim PM utterance that named execution. The FOURTH field of the stamp: plan-execute-session-split.md § Pinned conventions pins the stamp as a byte-identical FOUR-field contract (by/at/sha/note); note is the self-attesting field — a stamp without a note that names execution signals the write-bar may not have been met. Do NOT drop it. OPTIONAL, mirrored from handoff.schema.json's identically-named field for the plan→execute-plan Stop-hook seam. Spec backlink: pln-first-class-execution-handoff--40a6e5 § C1

status_override_by.description: The session that overrode the completeness verdict when stamping `status: implemented`. OPTIONAL — one of the three-field override stamp (by/reason/at), written ONLY by `plan-status-transition stamp-implemented --override-reason`. Negative-spec: this stamp records an override of the SPINE/AC completeness verdict only; it never relaxes the live-foreign-holder refusal, which still runs unchanged. Supersedes the unschema'd hand-edit route (`status_stamped_by: EM-manual`, `status_stamped_by_hand`) that improvised two different field spellings across two repos because the engine offered no sanctioned path when it declined. Spec backlink: claude-klabauter:cross-repo/archive/2026-08-10-example-retrieval-repo-em-close-out-stamps-implemented-without-reading-the-ac-table.md

status_override_reason.description: The verbatim operator reason for overriding the completeness verdict. REQUIRED by the op whenever an override is taken — `--override-reason` refuses empty text, so a bare force with no stated cause cannot reach disk. OPTIONAL here in shape terms (absent on every non-override plan). One of the three-field override stamp (by/reason/at).

status_override_at.description: ISO 8601 date-time of the completeness-verdict override. OPTIONAL — one of the three-field override stamp (by/reason/at), written in the same locked_rmw mutate closure as the status flip it accompanies, so the stamp and the flip cannot diverge.

review_signals.description: Selects which reviewers this plan needs, forward — distinct from `reviewer`, which records who already approved it, backward. Values are not enumerated here by design — the vocabulary is `coordinator/contract/review-signals.json`, and membership is enforced by the contract's parity test plus the frontmatter write guard where a coordinator engine is installed.

review_verified_by.description: The session that recorded a code-review pass over the work this plan delivered. OPTIONAL — one of the three-field review attest (by/at/findings), written ONLY by `plan-status-transition` alongside a terminal `status: implemented`, in the same locked_rmw mutate closure as the flip it accompanies, so the attest and the status cannot diverge. Negative-spec: this is an attest, not a status — absence means no code review was recorded, never that a review failed, and nothing gates a close-out on it. Spec backlink: pln-a-plan-s-status-advances-itsel-fb8bf2 § C1(c).

review_verified_at.description: ISO 8601 date-time of the code-review pass. OPTIONAL — one of the three-field review attest (by/at/findings).

review_verified_findings.description: Path to the review-trail record the pass produced, e.g. `state/review-trail/findings/<date>-<slug>.md`. OPTIONAL — one of the three-field review attest (by/at/findings). A path, never a count: a count is a lossy copy of a record that already exists on disk and drifts from it. This value is also the attest's IDEMPOTENCE KEY — a re-run of the same wrap with an unchanged path writes nothing, while a genuine second review after fixes produces a new path and writes a fresh attest.

prime_exit_criterion.description: The plan-level falsifiable exit criterion — 'what is true of the tree when this plan has delivered', outcome-shaped per goal.schema.json's vocabulary. Deliberately NO `source`/provenance enum: a self-declared provenance flag is the unfalsifiable shape this plan (pln-plan-goal-as-a-first-class-exit-criterion) exists to remove. Provenance is instead `derived_from`, a LINK a reader can open and compare against, never an assertion. PROPORTIONALITY (enforced READ-SIDE, the same locus as `sizing_object`'s own cross-document requirement, never structurally in this file because `estimate.tshirt` lives in the external sizing-object document, not here): `falsifier` is REQUIRED only when the plan's `sizing_object` resolves to `estimate.tshirt` M/L/XL. At size S (spec-dispatch posture) a plan carries `statement`+`derived_from` only, no falsifier. XS never scaffolds a plan at all, so this object never appears. XXL routes to prime-exit-criterion-setting/roadmap, not a single plan; its obligation is discharged per-child-plan. The size carve-out keys ONLY on `estimate.tshirt` through `sizing_object` — never on an EM-set field, and never on plain field optionality: the shape below still marks `falsifier` absent from THIS object's own `required` array (JSON Schema cannot condition on a sibling document's content), but a plan sized M+ with no `falsifier` and no `falsifier_exemption` fails the read-side check even though it validates here. Do not read the schema-level optionality as the plan's own gate.

statement.description: One falsifiable sentence naming what is true of the tree when this plan has delivered. Outcome-shaped (a measurable change in behaviour or state), never output-shaped (a deliverable produced, a task list wearing this field's clothes).

derived_from.description: Provenance BY LINK, not by self-declaration: a path to the sizing object that routed this plan (`state/sizings/<id>.yaml`, same shape as this schema's own top-level `sizing_object` field) or a key-result reference (`<goal_id>#kr-<kr-id>`, e.g. `goal-shipping-velocity#kr-throughput`) naming a KR in `state/goals/*.yaml` this plan serves — `<goal_id>` is the target goal's `id` field and `<kr-id>` is that goal's `key_results[].id` (goal.schema.json), never an array index, exactly like `kr-suggestion.schema.json`'s own `goal_id`/`kr_id` anchors. Openable and comparable against `statement` — the corpus-existing `intent`/`intent_source` fields already carry what this points at; no new sizing-object field was added for it. A plan links to a KR it serves without the KR itself gaining a falsifier or an AC-table binding — one KR spans several plans, so this is a pointer, never a merge of the two documents.

falsifier.description: The plan-time-authored observation distinguishing the prime exit criterion being true from false, with its baseline captured BEFORE any work — authored by someone with no stake yet in the answer. This is NOT a typed cell and is NOT bound to the AC table: it is one observation per plan, EM-chosen free form (a command, a query, a measurement, a named manual observation), judged by a human reading the re-run against a stated pass condition, never a script's exit code or a `grep:`/`pytest:`/`sh:` typed cell. It is NOT the retired acceptance oracle: it is categorically different on five axes (cardinality, typing, chooser, judge, target artifact); see `docs/wiki/coordinator-tripwires/tripwire-registry/acceptance-oracle-gate-retired.md` for the retired mechanism this must not be reshaped back into, and do not 'improve' this field into a typed cell or delete it as a revival of that retirement. Mutually exclusive with `falsifier_exemption` — a prime exit criterion carries at most one of the two.

how.description: The observation that distinguishes the prime exit criterion being true from false. Form is the EM's choice — a command, a query, a measurement, a named manual observation. Bounded at 4096 chars: this lands raw in the plan's YAML frontmatter, where an unbounded payload is a corpus hazard and the frontmatter validator is lenient about coercions. Output over the bound means the falsifier is too wide, never that the record should be truncated — narrow the observation (a count, a filtered line set).

baseline_output.description: The raw output of `how`, run against HEAD before any work. Must show the prime exit criterion is currently FALSE — a baseline that already passes means the criterion is mis-stated, the work is already done, or the falsifier does not measure the criterion, all of which are worth catching at plan time. Bounded at 4096 chars: this lands raw in the plan's YAML frontmatter, where an unbounded payload is a corpus hazard and the frontmatter validator is lenient about coercions. Output over the bound means the falsifier is too wide, never that the record should be truncated — narrow the observation (a count, a filtered line set).

promoted_to.description: The test path this falsifier graduated into when it was executable and deterministic enough to become a standing regression pin. Promotion is REAL but never a gate: an unpromotable falsifier (a manual observation, a measurement against a live index) is not a lesser falsifier, and making promotability a precondition for the stamp would push EMs to choose falsifiers for their promotability rather than their discrimination. Mutually exclusive with `promotion`.

promotion.description: The recorded NON-promotion, for a falsifier that cannot graduate into the suite. Held to a single spelling so the field cannot become a free-text status. Requires `promotion_reason`. Mutually exclusive with `promoted_to`.

promotion_reason.description: Why this falsifier does not promote — a manual observation, a measurement against a live index, a one-shot migration check. Close-out accepts this and stamps; the reason is for a later reader deciding whether promotion became possible since.

baseline_ref.description: Where the baseline was taken (a commit sha). One falsifier per plan, one baseline_ref — never one per AC row, which would be per-item git-spawn amplification.

expected_when_true.description: What `how`'s observation yields WHEN the prime exit criterion is TRUE — the stated pass condition the close-out re-run is judged against. Makes the falsifier a discriminating observation, not a blob to diff: a re-run output is judged by whether it matches this shape/content, never by whether it merely differs from `baseline_output`. A non-null delta from baseline that still does not match `expected_when_true` is a criterion that is still false, differently. Bounded at 4096 chars for the same corpus-hazard reason as `how`/`baseline_output`.

falsifier_exemption.description: The NAMED escape hatch for an M+ prime exit criterion genuinely un-falsifiable-by-observation — pure doctrine/schema edits where 'run it and watch it fail' is contrived (this plan is itself in that class; see its own § This plan's own falsifier). Distinct from, and never a substitute for, the size carve-out: the size carve-out is a rule about which PLANS the instrument suits (keyed on `estimate.tshirt`), this is a rule about which M+ CRITERIA resist any instrument, and the two do not merge — a plan cannot claim exemption from `falsifier` by pointing at its size, nor claim the size carve-out by pointing at this exemption. NEVER `falsifier: optional`: this object exists precisely so optionality is never reopened as the way out. Mutually exclusive with `falsifier`.

class.description: The one admitted class, held to a single spelling so a later reader cannot widen it by inventing new class strings. Covers only work with no runtime behaviour to observe — doctrine prose, schema/contract shape edits with no executable surface a `how` could measure.

admission.description: The written admission test: a non-empty statement that (1) names why no baseline-red observation exists for this specific prime exit criterion, (2) confirms the change is doctrine/schema/contract-shaped with no runtime behaviour a falsifier could observe, and (3) is written by someone who first tried and failed to draft a `falsifier`, not someone who skipped the attempt. An admission that could be copy-pasted onto any plan without editing is not admissible — it must speak to THIS criterion.

gated_exit_criteria.description: The fleet brightlines, discharged as a machine-readable field on the plan artifact the executor holds rather than remembered from a doctrine page. Scaffolded in full by `coordinator/templates/plans/plan.md.tmpl`; a row is never deleted because it seems inapplicable, its `statement` is narrowed instead. Deliberately NOT a repeated `prime_exit_criterion`-shaped object: a full falsifier per brightline is per-item spawn amplification for a check that is almost always a direct read, so this stays a light three-field row and `prime_exit_criterion.falsifier` stays the one-per-plan heavy instrument. Deliberately NOT an `## Acceptance Criteria` table row either — that table is optional, reviewer-facing prose and is never mechanically gated, so a brightline landed there would be present but not gated, which is the exact failure this field exists to close.

brightline.description: A fixed slug. The enum is the mechanism: an ad-hoc slug is how a brightline becomes a freehand row nothing gates. A new brightline is a plan chunk that extends this enum and the template together, never a plan-local addition.

statement.description: Authored at plan-write time: what evidence at close-out would show this brightline held for THIS plan's delivered work. Same falsifiable-sentence discipline as `prime_exit_criterion.statement`, scoped to one brightline. `work-vs-question-ratio` is discharged by naming, per function or corpus-scale value the plan introduces, the bounded question it answers — an act, never the bare disposition "proportionate".

met.description: Starts `false` and is flipped only by the session writing `exit_criterion_met` — never pre-set `true` at authoring time. An unmet brightline blocks `implemented` the same way an unresolved prime exit criterion does, on that same close-out path; there is deliberately no second enforcement path.

exit_criterion_met.description: Written once, at close-out, by the EM — the assertion half of the prime-exit-criterion pair. `asserted: false` is a legitimate, first-class outcome (the plan is Phase-5-halted, not `implemented`); what is forbidden is the field's absence. Not bound to the AC table — see `prime_exit_criterion.falsifier`'s description for the acceptance-oracle distinction, which applies identically here.

asserted.description: Whether HEAD now satisfies `prime_exit_criterion.statement`. `false` is legitimate and takes `reason`; it is never omitted in place of a `false` value.

asserted_by.description: The session id of the EM that made the assertion. Names WHO looked, so an assertion is attributable rather than anonymous — route-c's stamp was made in good faith by an EM who had genuinely looked, and attribution is what lets a later reader ask them what they saw.

asserted_at.description: ISO-8601 date the assertion was made. Dates the observation, so a re-run against a much later HEAD is visibly not the same evidence.

falsifier_output.description: The SAME observation (`prime_exit_criterion.falsifier.how`) re-run against HEAD, raw. Judged against `prime_exit_criterion.falsifier.expected_when_true`, never against `baseline_output` alone — a changed output that still does not match `expected_when_true` is a criterion that is still false, differently, and unchanged output fails the same check without needing a separate rule. Bounded at 4096 chars: this lands raw in the plan's YAML frontmatter, where an unbounded payload is a corpus hazard and the frontmatter validator is lenient about coercions. Output over the bound means the falsifier is too wide, never that the record should be truncated — narrow the observation (a count, a filtered line set).

falsifier_verdict.description: The re-run's verdict: whether `falsifier_output` matches `prime_exit_criterion.falsifier.expected_when_true`. The gate refuses the stamp unless this is `pass`. Written beside `falsifier_output`, never inferred by a downstream reader from the raw output alone.

prose.description: The EM's own sentence tying the falsifier_output verdict to the prime exit criterion. The verdict is the evidence; this is the signature, not a substitute for it — an assertion with no falsifier output beside it is a checkbox.

reason.description: REQUIRED when `asserted: false`. What is not true of HEAD yet, and where the remainder is routed.

grouping_approvals.description: $comment: BLOCK PRESENCE IS THE WHOLE GOVERNED/LEGACY DISCRIMINATOR. A plan's frontmatter carrying this key at all makes the plan GOVERNED; a plan with no such key is LEGACY and keeps the existing per-row `pm_approved` gate unchanged. There is deliberately NO schema_version conjunct anywhere in this discriminator — do not add one. Presence-only is not taken bare, though: a GOVERNED plan whose `grouping_approvals` block is malformed, or that lacks the grouping a closed row needs, FAILS LOUD (schema violation here, plus the hard authorization check in schema_validate.py's check_plan_tasks_grouping_approval) — it does NOT silently degrade to legacy treatment. `additionalProperties: false` and `required: ["status"]` on each block (below) are what make a malformed block a structural violation rather than something that reads as merely absent. Groupings are DERIVED from each task-spine row's `disposition` and never stored separately: do <- open/coded; spun_off <- spun_off; defer <- backlogged; ruled_out <- wont_do. `spun_off` was split out of `defer` and relaxed by DoE's five-exits ruling (state/memo-outbox/sent/plan-tasks-five-exits-ruling.md, landed in claude-klabauter at f55daf8b9): moving a row to another plan drops no work, so it needs no PM ratification, while `backlogged` and `wont_do` do drop work and stay PM-gated. Plan-level approval is the SUM of the block statuses, COMPUTED at read time — never stored as a fourth rollup field (a stored rollup would be a second home for a derivable truth, and the two would drift). Mirrors claude-klabauter's vendored shape in coordinator_core/frontmatter/schemas/plan-tasks.schema.json (`$defs.grouping_approval_block`) — do not diverge from that spelling. Spec backlink: pln-pm-approved-gets-falsifiable-p-00737d § C1.

grouping_approval_block.description: One grouping_approvals grouping's approval state (do | defer | ruled_out). `pending` is the default, unapproved state. `approved` requires a non-empty `pm_utterance` (the PM's verbatim reasoning — testimonial, never backfilled/inferred) and a `digest` matching `sha256:<hex>` (a fresh recomputation over the CURRENT spine membership for this grouping — see schema_validate.py's compute_grouping_digest for the exact recipe). The `sha256:` prefix is load-bearing, never bare 40-hex hash: a membership digest names nothing in any git object store, so a bare-hex value would look like (and invite confusion with) a git object id, when the only valid operation on it is recompute-and-compare. `additionalProperties: false` plus `required: ["status"]` mean an unrecognized key or a missing `status` is a schema violation, not something that silently reads as an absent/legacy block.

approver.description: Who approved this grouping (PM identity/handle). Null while pending.

approved_at.description: Date this grouping was approved (YYYY-MM-DD). Null while pending.

pm_utterance.description: The PM's verbatim reasoning for approving this grouping. REQUIRED non-empty when status: approved (see allOf below). Never synthesized or backfilled — a grouping's assent is testimonial, not mechanically derivable from disk state.

digest.description: sha256:<hex> membership digest over the sorted set of (row id, disposition) pairs for the rows currently in this grouping, and nothing else. REQUIRED when status: approved (see allOf below). Row order, row body prose, section rendering, other frontmatter fields, and whitespace/YAML-style differences are all NOT covered.

allOf.$comment: Cross-field rule: status: approved requires non-empty pm_utterance and a well-formed digest. Presence-only / non-hard-failing at THIS schema layer — the hard truthiness/freshness check (does the digest match a FRESH recomputation? is pm_utterance non-empty, not just present?) is schema_validate.py's job (check_plan_tasks_grouping_approval), not this file's.
